newsitem.title: USA: Crown jewels moved from vault to Russian Embassy.
newsitem.headline: Crown jewels moved from vault to Russian Embassy.

text.p: Priceless crown jewels from Russia's imperial past that have been caught up in a standoff between Russia and American art lovers were moved on Monday from an art gallery vault to the Russian Embassy.

A spokeswoman for the Corcoran Gallery of Art, a stone's throw from the White House, said the crown jewels were moved by armoured car to the embassy. Where they go from there was the subject of bargaining but American and Russian negotiators hoped to reach an agreement on where the priceless pieces from Russia's czarist days should go next -- Russia or Texas.

"It's looking very hopeful," a spokeswoman for the American-Russian Cultural Cooperation Foundation said about the negotiations. A news conference to discuss the status of the talks was tentatively planned for later in the day.

For nearly two weeks now, negotiators from Russia and the American-Russian Cultural Foundation, which helped arrange an American tour of the artifacts, have been wrangling over the treasure's next destination. For 10 weeks until April 13, the jewels, costumes and art had been on view at the Corcoran before capacity crowds. More than 80,000 people paid $9 each.

The collection was then to be shipped to Houston for the next stop on what would be a nationwide tour. But the Russians balked, blocking a truck containing some of the artwork from moving until it was allowed last week to go to the Russian Embassy until the matter of the next stop was settled.
The czarist jewels remained in the Corcoran vault until Monday.

Russia has said it wanted the treasures back for Moscow's 850th birthday celebration in May, according to the Corcoran, but the American sponsors argued that would violate the agreement to bring the treasures here.
